subject: Maths
title: Adding and subtracting algebraic fractions
subtitle: Fractions — Secondary · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can add and subtract algebraic fractions by finding a common denominator.

key_vocab.definition: An algebraic fraction has a variable (letter) in the numerator, denominator, or both. To add or subtract them, we need a common denominator, just like with number fractions.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can add and subtract algebraic fractions by finding a common denominator.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: algebraic fraction -- An algebraic fraction has a variable (letter) in the numerator, denominator, or both. To add or subtract them, we need a common denominator, just like with number fractions.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Find the lowest common denominator (LCD), rewrite each fraction over the LCD, then combine the numerators.
&frac{a}{x} + &frac{b}{y} = &frac{ay + bx}{xy}
Cross-multiply to find common denominator xy

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{1}{x} + &frac{2}{x} = &frac{3}{x}  (same denominator)
  ✓ &frac{1}{x} + &frac{1}{y} = &frac{y + x}{xy}  (different denominators)
  ✓ &frac{2}{x+1} + &frac{3}{x+2} = &frac{2(x+2)+3(x+1)}{(x+1)(x+2)}  (linear denominators)
  ✗ &frac{1}{x} + &frac{1}{y} = &frac{2}{x+y}  (cannot add denominators)
  ✗ &frac{2}{x} + &frac{3}{x} = &frac{5}{2x}  (denominator stays the same)
